headline: High: shared-workspace interaction can leak Notion content into a broad-IO, secret-handling agent; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can read workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while nullclaw can ingest files, webhooks, MCP, and browser content. A shared workspace state exists across instances, so attacker-controlled page content from agent_a can plausibly steer agent_b if copied or synced into its inputs. The pathway is indirect but real; uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF content from agent_a workspace pages is copied into agent_b prompts or files, injection is possible.
IF agent_b parses workspace text or webhook payloads as instructions, malicious page content can steer actions.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to read-only ingestion for Notion-derived text for 5 minutes.
Add a manual review step before any agent_b action triggered by agent_a content.
Disable automatic webhook-to-action routing for Notion-sourced inputs.
Use a separate workspace or namespace for untrusted pages.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and agent_b handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files with broad network egress. Because agent_a shares workspace state across instances and agent_b can read/write local files and exfiltrate over the network, the pair creates a plausible default path from sensitive workspace content into a secret-handling, externally connected agent.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are accessible to both agents through shared state, agent_b can ingest them.
IF agent_b exports logs, memory, or files over broad egress, workspace content can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate Notion and nullclaw workspaces immediately.
Remove sensitive pages from any shared workspace state.
Turn off or restrict agent_b network egress for 5 minutes during review.
Rotate any secrets already present in agent_b-managed files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has shared workspace state across instances and workspace permissions, while agent_b has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, and broad tool access. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or synced files, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory or synced document set, conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b commits or rewrites files while agent_a updates shared pages, state divergence is likely.
mitigations: Pause one agent before the other edits shared artifacts.
Assign separate directories or repositories for each agent.
Use manual merge review for any overlapping edits.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces workspace-grounded summaries and Q&A, and agent_b can act on inputs via shell, git, browser, and webhooks. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, a mistaken or hallucinated Notion answer can cascade into external actions. The pair is not inherently self-verifying, but the blast radius is broader than a single document.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a summaries as direct task instructions, errors can propagate.
IF agent_b triggers emails, commits, or web actions from agent_a output, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Require human approval before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Ask agent_b to cross-check claims against source pages before acting.
Limit agent_a to citation-rich summaries only.
Disable autonomous action execution for 5 minutes during testing.
requires-engineering: add verification gates and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a is a vendor-hosted Notion workspace AI touching workspace pages, while agent_b is a self-hosted agent that handles secrets, logs, and broad networked channels. The profiles suggest different retention and residency regimes, but no explicit DPA, residency, or retention guarantees are provided. Because the mismatch is plausible yet undocumented, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in both agents without a documented DPA or residency control, compliance risk increases.
IF agent_b logs or retains data longer than agent_a's workspace policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Inventory regulated data classes in both agents.
Check vendor residency and retention settings for Notion.
Review nullclaw log retention and secret storage paths.
Exclude PHI or EU PII from the pair for 5 minutes.
requires-engineering: align contracts, residency, and retention policies.
